title: Maukhari Dynasty
capsule: The Maukhari dynasty was the dominant power in the central Gangetic plains in the post-Gupta period, ruling from their capital at Kanyakubja (Kannauj) from around 550 CE. Ishanavarman (c. 554–574) was the first Maukhari ruler to claim the title Maharajadhiraja and is credited with defeating Hunnic forces in the Doab, a claim supported by the Aphsad inscription that attributes the Huna defeat primarily to the Maukharis rather than the Guptas. King Sharvavarman (c. 574–586) exchanged diplomatic missions with the Sasanian emperor Khosrow I, reportedly sending chess sets to Persia. The last Maukhari ruler, Grahavarman, was killed by Devagupta of Malwa around 605–606 CE, and the dynasty's territories were absorbed into the empire of Harsha Vardhana, whose sister had married Grahavarman.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Maukhari dynasty's core territory around Kannauj is attested through copper-plate inscriptions and the Harsha Charita, but the precise extent of their control over adjacent regions of UP and Bihar at any given point is inferred rather than directly documented.
